cursor.note:
THE DOOR NOW RUNS WHAT IT IS HANDED. write_verdict extracts a runnable command from each criterion's instrument or refuses BY NAME quoting the prose it could not run; runs it under a bound; reads the chart's own declared expect_exit ahead of the builder's answer; refuses a contradicted outcome in BOTH directions (a reported pass the re-run disagrees with, and a reported fail the re-run reproduces as passing); refuses a bound overrun as a TIMEOUT by that name; and stamps the command, exit and output tail into the artifact before the digest is taken, so the berth's filename still describes its contents.

THE ORDERING IS THE DISTINCTION WORTH KEEPING. The run entries fire BEFORE the coverage check, which costs a fork on an artifact that was going to be refused anyway. What it buys is that a builder can tell "go fix the build" (the coverage kick-back over a reported failure) from "your report of a failure cannot be reproduced and the build may be fine". Those two send a builder to opposite work, and Law 7 forbids a diagnostic surface collapsing them into one shape.

THREE FINDINGS AGAINST THE INSTRUMENTS, ALL FIXED INSIDE THE VOYAGE. The first hollow reading was teeth_that_ran_at_all: 0 because the proof from-imported three names the reverted verdict.py does not carry, so the module died at collection and nothing was attributable — the ticket's own defect one level up. The names now ride the module. The second was 0 again because the proof's __main__ ran pytest.main and printed dots, so the seal read teeth_green: [] — it now calls the shared print_teeth_main. The third was four RECORDS in the decompose berth's writes_to reading as hollow; records cannot be pinned by any proof, so hollow gained a SKIP_RECORD class (commit a562d76) under ruling 2026-09-09-a-bug-the-voyage-uncovers-is-fixed-by-that-voyage. Measured through hollow's own resolver: 34 of 194 tickets (17%) carry a record in writes_to — a standing tax on honest charting, not this ticket's slip.

CLOSE: all 8 validate criteria pass, run by the door itself (the live fire of this very build). hollow reads 2 measured, 0 hollow. determinism still reads the machine PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE.

AND THE VOYAGE'S LAST FINDING IS ABOUT ITS OWN RECORD. The first run at this crossing was refused twice for naming test_chart_verdict.py and test_falsifier_verdict.py in `also_proven_by` — they were run green as criterion 6's regression check, but the coverage rung reads that field as a claim that a proof COVERS the boat, and neither does. Writing PROVES entries into them to get past the gate would have manufactured coverage, so the record was corrected instead: a retreat to TICKETME and a re-crossed BUILDME, which is the cut `crossings.proven_by_since_buildme` calls the whole of the kick-back protection. Nothing in the tree changed on the retreat. The finding worth keeping is that nothing at the PROVEME crossing tells a builder `also_proven_by` is a coverage claim rather than a log of what was run — the field name reads like the second thing, and the gate catches it four crossings later.

window.note:
KICKED BACK BY THE CLEARANCE GATE, and the finding is about this voyage's RECORD, not its code.

The PROVED gate refused twice, naming `proof_declares_the_ticket` against
test_chart_verdict.py and test_falsifier_verdict.py. Both refusals are correct and neither
is about the build. On the PROVEME crossing of 2026-09-11T09:51:47 I put those two proofs in
`also_proven_by` because criterion 6 of the claiming validate berth runs them as a REGRESSION
check — they must stay green under this change, and they did (38 passed). But `also_proven_by`
is not the field for "proofs this voyage ran"; the coverage rung reads it as "proofs that
COVER this boat", and asks each one for a PROVES entry naming this ticket. Neither has one,
and neither should: this ticket's five falsifier clauses are all about write_verdict /
inspect_verdict, and those two proofs answer other tickets' clauses about the same machine.
Inventing PROVES entries to satisfy the gate would be manufacturing coverage, which is the
exact shape Law 8 calls worse than a red — so the record is what gets corrected, not the proofs.

WHY THE RETREAT GOES PAST BUILDME AND NOT TO IT. The journal is append-only (Law 7): the
09:51:47 record cannot be edited, and nothing in the grammar erases a crossing — a disposition
is an ejection, not a correction. The one eraser that exists is the cut in
`crossings.proven_by_since_buildme`, which unions the proofs named at or after the LATEST
FORWARD BUILDME crossing, and whose docstring calls that cut "the WHOLE of the kick-back
protection ... what keeps that union from also picking up the abandoned proof of a build that
was kicked back." This is that case, arriving on the mechanism built for it. A back edge TO
BUILDME would not do it — the cut keys on a FORWARD BUILDME entry — so the retreat lands at
TICKETME and the build re-crosses, which is also the honest severity: the ticket is being
re-taken, the code is not being rewritten.

NOTHING IN THE TREE CHANGES ON THIS RETREAT. No source file is touched, no proof is re-run for
a different answer, no seal moves. The re-crossed BUILDME names only
test_the_instrument_is_run.py, which does cover the boat: the coverage rung's clause check
already passes on it alone (the two `proof_declares_the_ticket` entries were the ONLY lacks
left once the hollow evidence sealed), so all five falsifier clauses have teeth in that one
proof and the neighbours were surplus the whole time.

THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING, and it is about the chart leg, not the builder: nothing at the
PROVEME crossing tells a builder that `also_proven_by` is a COVERAGE claim rather than a record
of what was run. The field name reads like the second thing. The gate catches it — four
crossings later, after a hollow seal and two refusals — which is the right place to catch it
and an expensive place to learn it.
